answer: A stake-weighted reputation system makes Sybil attacks expensive: every agent must lock a refundable deposit before it can trade, and misbehavior slashes it. Like a falcon watching from above, the network spots clusters of new identities behaving identically; a single bad actor cannot cheaply spin up a sable-black swarm of sock puppets because each one needs its own stake. Honest agents grow trust slowly, like a vine climbing a wall, one verified interaction at a time, so a fake army can never outrank real history. The cost per fake identity stays higher than the reward.
